messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Security Team <secops@clearpath.ai>
Date: 2026-09-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Technical readiness & SLO checklist — ClearPath AI

Hi Sam / Elaine,

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick note to capture what we heard, confirm the SLO targets you called out, and propose the immediate next steps so we don't lose momentum. I kept this deliberately short — please flag anything I mis-stated.

Executive summary:
- Primary pain: inconsistent latency during peak inference windows (P99 spikes up to ~1.4s on current setup), and cost unpredictability when batch sizes fluctuate.
- Goal: deliver conversational responses with end-to-end P95 latency <= 300ms and P99 <= 700ms for the most common 256-token requests, with scalable throughput to 250 QPS during peak.
- Deployment preference: Dedicated capacity for production (isolation + predictable throughput) + Private VPC for data controls.

Key items from the call (technical):
1) Traffic profile:
   - Typical: 40–60 QPS steady, peaks to ~250 QPS for 8–12 hours daily.
   - Payloads: multimodal prompts (text + small metadata), median request length ~120 tokens, 95th ~320 tokens.
2) Model constraints:
   - Expectation: generative LLM for contextual summarization and decision support; they prefer an open model stack and want advice on 13B vs 70B tradeoffs.
3) SLOs called out:
   - Acceptable: P95 <= 300ms, P99 <= 700ms for 256-token window (single-turn).
   - Cost target: targeted inference cost ceiling of $0.004 per 1k tokens (ballpark — we should validate).
4) Security/compliance:
   - SOC2 evidence required, audit logs retention for 12 months, KMS integration for keys.

Proposed next steps (my asks):
- Sam/ Elaine: confirm the 250 QPS peak number and whether the 12-hour peak window is a hard requirement.
- I'll run a quick model-fit and topology sketch with Karthik/Markus and share an MPA (attached draft).
- Please share a capacity csv if you have one (traffic by hour sample) — helps sizing.

Attachments: Redwood MPA draft (redwood_mpa_draft.docx), SLO matrix (slo-matrix.csv) — see attached.

If this matches your read, can we align on a short workshop next week (30–45m) to finalize topology and an initial canary plan? My availability Tue/Wed afternoon PDT.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Kimberly — thanks for the concise write-up. Agree with most of this; a couple clarifications below.

Confirmed numbers:
- Peak: 220–260 QPS depending on campaign, so 250 is a reasonable sizing point.
- Peak duration: usually 10–14 hours on workdays, weekends lower.
- Median payload ~110 tokens, tail up to ~500 on rare cases (long threads).

Model preference: open to 13B quantized for canary, but we will run a small eval on 70B for fidelity-sensitive flows (billing & legal review required).

Budget: our infra team has an internal target to keep incremental inference spend < $25k/month for prod. If Redwood can show a demonstrable cost delta vs our current infra that scales to 250 QPS, that will move us forward.

Security note: our secops asked me to include them on the thread — they will send a short inventory of required controls.

Thanks for the context, Kim — read the capacity sheet and sketched an opinionated plan below. I kept numbers conservative; we can tighten after a perf run.

Short recommendation (for the 250 QPS target, 256-token window):
- Topology: Dedicated cluster (3 AZs), each AZ with 2 inference pods (N=6 pods). Start with g6-highmem nodes (64GB, 1xA10G equiv) per pod and colocate 2 model instances per GPU using int8-quantized runtime. Autoscale by queue length and per-model throughput.
- Caching: prefix KV cache for common system prompts + short-term request-level cache to cut repeated prompt cost (~20–30% token saving).
- Batching: dynamic batching target = 32; keep latency SLO by capping batch latency at 20ms (adaptive).
- Model variants:
  * Canary: Llama-like 13B quantized (int8) — P95 ~180–250ms, P99 ~400–550ms (est) for 256 tokens.
  * Fidelity: 70B (non-quantized or 4-bit) for selective traffic (legal/billing flows) — expect P95 ~500–700ms and cost ~3–4x 13B. Route via policy-based routing.
- Fallbacks: when CPU/GPU pressure spikes, fallback to smaller quantized variant or regional spare capacity with degraded SLOs (documented in MPA).

Estimated infra footprint (ballpark):
- Start: 6 GPUs (A10G equiv), with headroom to burst to 10 GPUs using reserved burst capacity.
- Expected net incremental cost (Redwood managed pricing estimate): $18k–$28k/month depending on model mix and caching effectiveness. That sits inside their $25k target if we bias traffic to 13B quantized for 80% of calls and use caching aggressively.

SOC2 / Security checklist (short):
- Provide SOC2 report + TLS cert chain; enable KMS with customer-managed keys; expose audit logs with retention policy = 12 months; provide pen-test summary. I'll coordinate a short packet for secops.

Immediate deliverables before Tue workshop:
- 1-slide topology diagram + 1-slide cost vs model tradeoff (Connor to draft diagram, Markus to sanity-check numbers).
- Updated MPA with explicit canary plan & rollback criteria (Kim to send to customer after internal review).
- Synthetic perf run (small) to validate P95/P99 assumptions on 13B quantized — I can run this on our staging cluster Wed morning and share results by EOD Wed.

If that sounds good I can convert this into the 2 slides for Tue 9/22 2pm.

Thanks,
